payload.scope:
i8b takes on:
- A top-middle board toolbar of small icons: a greyed book placeholder (until i6) and an active phone-connect icon.
- The connect action: clicking phone-connect generates the ntfy topic pair, writes ~/.se/<project>/phone.json (enabled), and renders a locally-encoded QR in the details pane.
- The offer-reappear fix: a blessed or dismissed offer stays gone (red-first test).
- The refine machine-variant: seed from systematic, strike M2/M4/M5, and switch i8b's own machine to it so its remaining walk is genuinely short.
All against the existing i8 bless mechanics, unchanged.
payload.non_goals:
- The book itself and its open action (i6; the icon ships greyed).
- Other toolbar icons (future, per feature).
- Non-ntfy channels.
- The i8 bless mechanics themselves (unchanged).
- QR decoding / the inbound side (the phone app subscribes; we only encode a subscribe link).
- The general lean strike-list over any machine (se.req-lean-strike's broader scope; i8b realizes only the refine cut).
- Live from-away pairing with the owner's real device (owner-physical; se.raid-phone-live-pairing).
- Board consolidation beyond the toolbar (i9); the ETA-on-steps redesign (owner discussion).
payload.prfaq:
PRESS RELEASE (internal): Pair your phone in one click. The se board gains a phone-connect button - click it, a QR appears in the details pane, scan it with your ntfy app, and your phone is paired. Gate offers now reach your pocket and one tap blesses them from away. No config files, no typing secret topics; the topic is generated and drawn locally and never leaves your machine.

HOSTILE FAQ:
- Isn't a QR carrying a secret a leak? The QR is encoded locally and shown only on your own board; the topic IS the credential, exactly as the accepted authenticity model (se.adr-answer-authenticity) already rules.
- Why not a hosted QR service? That hands the topic to a third party. Refused.
- Does this add a heavy dependency? No - one-click install is the law (se.adr-install-over-zerodep); the encoder is vendored or hand-rolled and vetted at ship (se.meth-dependency-ship-review).
- Is the phone now required? No - the lane stays opt-in; without phone.json it is silent, unchanged from i8.
- Did you change how a bless is authenticated? No - i8's hash-bound, channel-stamped bless is untouched; i8b only adds the pairing gesture.
payload.findings_folded: None, with reason: no test or spike has run at M1. The first spike is the QR encoder at M6, and the red-first tests (reappear fix, connect action) land at M7. There is nothing upstream to fold at this state.
